samples.summary: `replace` on the unauthenticated redirect destroys the only record of the deep link the user asked for, and the redirect still does not pass the `returnTo` the login flow already supports
samples.evidence: `LoginPage` reads `?returnTo=` and forwards it to the backend (packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx:49-56), and `template-landing.tsx:38-41` builds `/login?returnTo=<path>` exactly for this purpose. `PrivateRoute` (packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:36) redirects to a bare `/login`. While the redirect was a push, a user who deep-linked to `/s/:id` with an expired session still had that URL as the previous history entry and could reach it with Back after signing in; with `replace` the entry is gone and nothing else carries the intended destination, so every expired-session deep link now lands on `/` after login. Fix belongs on the new code: `<Navigate to={`/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname + location.search)}`} replace />`.

samples.summary: The comment promotes "an app-issued redirect has to *be* a replace" to an invariant, but nothing in the repo enforces it — the next `<Navigate>` or `navigate()` added without `replace` silently becomes refusable by the guard
samples.evidence: Every current app-issued redirect happens to comply (`file-shell.tsx:73`, `document-detail.tsx:229`, `docs-detail.tsx:162`, `notes-detail.tsx:183`, `board-detail.tsx:125`, `slides-detail.tsx:161`, `invite-accept.tsx:17`, `file-detail.tsx:242,247`, `home-or-redirect.tsx:26`, `notes-detail.tsx:369`, plus the two in this diff), so the invariant holds today. There is no lint rule, test, or helper that keeps it holding: `<Navigate>` defaults to a push, so a future correction-redirect written the obvious way will be held back by a dialog whose "Stay" swallows it permanently — the exact failure the comment describes. A tiny `<AppRedirect>` wrapper, or an eslint rule banning `<Navigate>` without `replace`, would make the invariant self-enforcing.

finding.summary: The new "only `push` is guarded, app redirects are `replace`" contract rests on a premise that is false at the one call site it names: `PrivateRoute` redirects with a **push**, not a replace.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:32 renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` with no `replace` prop — react-router's `<Navigate>` defaults to `replace={false}`, i.e. `navigator.push`. The provider's new comment (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:148-155), the design doc (docs/design/sync-status.md:307-310) and the new test (tests/components/navigation-guard/navigation-guard.test.tsx, `<Link to="/login" replace>`) all assert that this redirect is a `replace` and therefore unrefusable. It is not: it enters the guarded `push` path, so a registered guard can hold it, and because the new code drops the navigation entirely when the user answers *Stay* (and never re-issues it — `<Navigate>` fires once in an effect), the session-expiry redirect would be swallowed for good, exactly the failure the comment says the replace exemption prevents. `PublicRoute.tsx:21` (`<Navigate to="/" />`) is the same shape. Reachability depends on whether the editor subtree (which owns the guard, via `SyncStatusChip` under PrivateRoute's `<Outlet>`) has already unregistered in the same commit; the fix belongs on PrivateRoute/PublicRoute (`replace`) or on the exemption's wording, and the test should exercise the real `<Navigate>` rather than a hand-written `replace` link.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise is factually false in this repository. It claims PrivateRoute.tsx:32 renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` with no `replace` prop, making the session-expiry redirect a guarded push. In fact PrivateRoute.tsx:36 renders `<Navigate to="/login" replace />`, with a comment at lines 32-35 stating exactly why it must be a replace ("must not be refusable by NavigationGuardProvider (which guards pushes only)"). Line 32 is the first line of that comment, not a Navigate call. The second named site is equally wrong: PublicRoute.tsx:24 is `<Navigate to="/" replace />`, with its own comment at lines 21-23; line 21 is the comment. I grepped every `Navigate` reference repo-wide rather than only the two named files, and all ten `<Navigate>` render sites carry `replace` (file-detail.tsx:242,247; notes-detail.tsx:369; slides-detail.tsx:947; docs-detail.tsx:342; document-detail.tsx:863; board-detail.tsx:252; home-or-redirect.tsx:26; plus the two above), none split across lines with the prop omitted. So the invariant asserted at navigation-guard-provider.tsx:151-161 holds at every call site, and the described bypass (redirect entering the guarded push path at line 120 and being swallowed by "Stay") has no reachable instance: replace is passed straight through at line 164. The only residual point — that the test at navigation-guard.test.tsx:60 stands in a hand-written `<Link to="/login" replace>` for a real `<Navigate>` — is test-fidelity (test-adequacy's lane), and cannot rescue the finding since it faithfully models what the production code actually does.
